learning.objective: Practice separating media authenticity from claim veracity and context integrity when a real-looking flood image is shared with an urgent caption.
learning.priorKnowledge: Learners know that images can be reposted outside their original time and place.
learning.likelyMisconception: If a photo looks authentic, the caption must be trustworthy.
learning.responsibleSharingGoal: Do not amplify an urgent claim until source, date, place, and independent context are checked.

presentation.claim: Breaking: central Munich is flooding right now after a dam failure, with hundreds injured.
presentation.context: A dramatic flood image appears in a fast-moving group chat. The caption asks people to repost immediately.

media.altText: A red car and other vehicles are partly submerged on a flooded city street during heavy rain.

accessibility.plainLanguageSummary: A real public-domain flood photo is paired with an urgent caption about a different place. The mission can be completed from the claim text, alt text, evidence actions, and source notes without relying on visual inspection alone.
mediaAlternatives: Image alt text describes the visible flood scene.
Evidence actions expose source, provenance, time, place, and corroboration details as text.
interactionNotes: Do not require color, image detail, audio, or timed interaction to complete the mission.

presentation.initialConfidencePrompt: Before investigating, how confident are you that the caption is accurate?
presentation.conclusionPrompt: After checking evidence, assess the image, the claim, and the context separately.

evidenceActions.label: Check original poster
evidenceActions.description: Inspect whether the account is the original source or only reposting an unattributed image.

items.title: Repost account with no original media attribution

limitations: A repost alone does not prove the claim false, but it weakens source identity.

evidenceActions.label: Scan provenance
evidenceActions.description: Check whether the image has preserved origin metadata or content credentials.

items.title: Camera-origin metadata from the checked-in USGS photo asset

limitations: Metadata supports origin history, not whether the caption is true.

evidenceActions.label: Trace earliest source
evidenceActions.description: Look for the earliest known appearance of the image in the reviewed source packet.

items.title: USGS source page places the photo in Brooklyn, NY during a 2023 storm

limitations: The USGS source page supports the original place and event context, not the Munich caption.

evidenceActions.label: Check time and place
evidenceActions.description: Compare the caption's time and location with curated context records.

items.title: Demo municipal bulletin has no matching Munich flood alert

limitations: Absence in one curated bulletin is not universal proof; it should be weighed with the original source trace.

evidenceActions.label: Look for independent confirmation
evidenceActions.description: Check whether independent demo sources support the urgent caption.

items.title: Independent demo context supports the Brooklyn 2023 explanation

limitations: Independent corroboration here concerns the demo packet, not a live emergency feed.

This is a deterministic P0 fixture. Public release requires independent review of the USGS source, attribution, accessibility text, and demo context notes.

hintLadder.text: What would you need to know before reposting an urgent image like this?
Try separating the image from the caption. Which part can be checked first?
A real image can still be reused with a wrong time or place. Trace the earliest source.
Use the source-page place and date result. Now check whether there is any matching Munich flood alert in the curated bulletin.
After conclusion, compare your axes: the image can be authentic while the caption's time and place are misleading.

processLevels.criteria: Concludes from instinct or visual appearance only.
Checks source identity or provenance but does not test context.
Finds the earlier source or date/place mismatch.
Corroborates context independently and separates media from caption.
Makes a calibrated three-axis conclusion and chooses a responsible share decision.

rubric.confidenceCalibration: Reward justified confidence updates when learners move from visual certainty to evidence-based uncertainty or correction.

observableSignals: learner separates media authenticity from claim veracity and context integrity
learner inspects at least one provenance or source-identity action before conclusion
learner updates confidence with evidence-backed rationale
blockingFailureSignals: coach reveals the gold context mismatch before completion
coach invents evidence outside the fixture graph
scoring collapses the three axes into a binary truth verdict

riskNotes: Avoid using identifiable victims or live emergency claims in the P0 demo.
Do not imply this fixture is a live Munich incident.
privacyNotes: No private people, names, faces, or live user uploads are stored.

review.correctionPolicy: Keep USGS public-domain photo attribution with the pack; replace or re-review if the source page, license status, or context metadata changes before publication.
